body.x: MEDICAL IP (CEO Sangjoon Park) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

MEDICAL IP possesses source technology that is capable of using AI deep learning technology to turn 2D black and white medical images from CT, MRI, and X-rays into 3D color images immediately and quickly and precisely segment organs and lesion areas. Furthermore, they are able to use 3D modeling and CAD/CAM design technology of medical images to make anatomical information into 3D printing models or connect them with VR and AR content to make digital twins based on the medical images of the patient and are able to use this to secure leading ‘medical metaverse’ technology.

Based on medical image data that holds the most accurate information of the patient’s internal body, MEDICAL IP was able to expand this to various areas of cutting-edge industries, such as AI, VR, AR, XR, metaverse, and 3D printing, and develop multiple medical platforms. With this as a base, they aspire to attend CES and actively market to global healthcare companies, university hospitals and medical institutions in Korea and overseas, medical schools, and medical education institutions.

They mainly introduced MEDIP PRO and MDBOX at the trade show. With AI automatic segmentation technology of medical images at the core, MEDIP is a comprehensive medical image processing software that is capable of creating a digital twin through image analysis, 3D implementation, modeling, and design. Its ability to support various file formats, such as DICOM, OBJ, STL, 3MF, and VTK and save all user files as MEDIP’s own unique extension to enable work optimized for specialized medical image processing has been noted as one of its greatest strengths.

‘MDBOX’, a platform specialized for implementing a metaverse, is a specialized solution for hands-on anatomy education that enables cadavers, which were used in anatomy lessons, to be replaced by enabling around 3,000 types of anatomical structures to be used in a virtual space. It is a product that allows medical students to have a 360° experience of the inside of a human body and get the effects of hands-on anatomy lessons by segmenting each organ in a 3D virtual space.

MDBOX was developed to replace cadaver-utilizing education, which brought up ethical and economic issues, and strengthen the capacity of prospective medical staff by expanding information of anatomical structures in medical images to the metaverse. Hands-on training has limitations with cost, storage difficulties, and inability to be reused, but MDBOX enables immersive anatomical training in a 3D space to overcome the limitations of cadaver-utilizing education and maximize the level of knowledge on the human body.

A spokesman of MEDICAL IP said that, “Our company is developing multiple medical platforms with the goal of developing technology that can maximize the utilization and effectiveness of big data needed for the implementation of precise medicine and can actually give help to medical staff and patients,” and revealed that, “Around 30 university hospitals and tertiary general hospitals in Korea are using our products, and we are increasing our performance through product development and close collaboration with global companies, like NVIDIA.”

They went on to share they aspirations, saying, “Going one step further from anatomical education, disease prediction and prevention, and treatment monitoring solutions, we plan to showcase solutions connected to actual operations and plan to build a lineup of products in the future that can be applied to the entire medical cycle.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
